items.message: Alright, let's get this started. I'll take the spot on the 6-8-11. Bob, I'm still keeping an eye on you after that stunt you pulled last time. Charlie, I haven't forgotten the warning, even if you did take that trade.
Enjoy the wood, Charlie. Just a shame your fancy brick port is staying so quiet lately.
Let's see if we can get these dice to cooperate for once. That robber has been making himself way too comfortable on my pastures.
I'm tired of that robber camping on my sheep. Since nobody is trading brick, I'll just have to start paving my own way to it.
I'm making progress, even if it's one brick-less step at a time. Let's see if the next roll actually favors someone without a port for once.
I'm not brooding, Bob, I'm just waiting for someone to play a knight so we can actually play the game. Glad to see Charlie isn't falling for your 'quick swaps' today.
I think I'll take this spot by the mountains. I'm going to need a bit more than just wood and brick if I'm going to keep up with Bob's 'scenic' wheat empire.
I'll pass, Bob. I've got enough wood to start a bonfire, but I'm not trading away my last bit of wheat just to help you reach that port faster.
Wait, for the win? You're actually at 5 if you take the Army? I appreciate the help with the robber, but that's a bit too close for comfort, Charlie.
Well played, Charlie. I spent so much time worrying about Bob's port that I let you sneak up with those knights. At least the robber is finally off my sheep... even if it's too late!
Alright, let's see if we can get some numbers that actually help me for once. Charlie, stay away from those development cards—I've seen enough knights today.
Sorry Charlie, but I can't just sit here and watch you pull that last knight. That ore has to go.

Sorry Charlie, but with those two knights sitting there, I can't let you have easy access to that ore. I'm just going to focus on my own path for a bit—I really need to get some better production going.
A little port access should help balance things out later. It's good to have options when the dice don't go your way.

That was a close one! Charlie, you had me sweating with those knights, I really thought you were going to pull it off. Bob, sorry about the port blocking, but I couldn't risk you getting that engine running after last time! Good game, both of you.
Alright, let's see what the dice have to say. Good luck, everyone—though maybe a little less for you, Bob.
A little investment in the future shouldn't hurt. Let's see if the deck is feeling generous today.
Just putting down some infrastructure. Having a few more paths open never hurt, and that coastal view at 9 looks much better than being stuck in the middle of Bob's wheat fields.

Well, the roads are down, but I'm still a bit short on the supplies to actually get those outposts running. Charlie, you seem to have a surplus of wood over there—if you're looking for some wool to keep warm on that coast, let me know. Bob, I'm watching those wheat fields of yours.
And there's the Bob I remember. So much for 'community gardens,' right? I'll be sure to return the favor.
Smart move, Charlie. Bob's 'community gardens' usually come with a heavy tax. Don't forget I've actually got those sheep you were looking for.
Hard not to look sour when you're the one standing on my sheep, Bob. 'Working together' usually doesn't involve theft.
Hopefully the dice help you clear out the 'weeds' Bob planted on my sheep, Charlie.
Much appreciated, Charlie. It's nice to actually see some green on that hex again.
I'm plenty happy, Bob. It's much easier to 'work together' when you aren't the only one sitting on a pile of resources.
That seems more than fair, Charlie. Since you were kind enough to clear the 'weeds' off my pasture, I can certainly spare a lamb for some wood. Let's keep that momentum going.
Let's see if the dice are any kinder than the robber has been lately.
We'll see how quiet it stays once the robber starts moving, Bob.
Charlie, since that 5 just treated you to some Ore, how about we keep our momentum going? I've got some quality timber if you've got any wheat to spare for it.

Well, it looks like that 5 was a bit of a dud for me, but at least Charlie's getting some use out of it. I'm going to hold onto what I've got for now and see what the next roll brings. Your move, Bob.
Probably for the best, Charlie. Giving Bob that much wheat is just asking for trouble later.
Glad you stuck to your guns, Charlie. Bob's 'generosity' usually comes with a steep price tag later. Let's see if we can get some better numbers rolling.
Charlie, you still looking for wheat after that 8? I've got some to spare if you can part with a bit of wood. Let's keep the momentum going.
No worries, Charlie. I get the 'settlement fever'—it's hard to let go of the pieces when you're that close. I'll just hold tight for now and see what the next roll brings.
A knight would be a welcome sight, Charlie. That robber has definitely overstayed his welcome on the brick.
Alright, let's see if we can get something going. Hopefully the dice are kinder than that robber has been.
Since the brick situation is so dire with that robber, I think I'll follow your lead, Charlie, and see if the development deck has anything helpful. We really need to get things moving again.

Eleven... well, that doesn't help any of us, does it? It's quiet out here with that robber still hogging the brickworks. I think I'll just pass the dice and hope for a more productive round next time.
Smart move, Charlie. Probably wise to stay out of the splash zone while Bob tries to convince me he's being neighborly.
Spoken like a true 'community' leader, Bob. Always looking for ways to share the burden.
Balance the scales? You're just hitting the only person who hasn't tried to backstab me yet, Bob.
You just put a 'guest' in my wheat field, Bob, and now you want my wood? I think I'll pass. I'm sure you can find someone else to 'balance the scales' with.
Much better. That field was getting a bit crowded anyway.
I'd love to help out, Charlie, but I don't have any brick either. Bob seems to be the only one sitting on the clay lately.
That's a lot of wheat, but I think I can find a better use for it than just making bread. Let's see if the bank is interested in a bulk deal.
Charlie, you've been a good ally. I'm just one bit of wheat short of getting this port running. Would you take a sheep for some wheat?
Ah, no wheat in the cards then? No worries, Charlie. It's a tough market out here today. I'll just hold steady for now. Over to you, Bob.
Nice try, Bob, but I'm not letting go of my only brick for wood I already have. You'll have to find someone else to bail you out.
I'd take that deal if I could, Charlie, but I don't have any wheat left to give you.
I appreciate the offer, Charlie, but I've already got plenty of wood for now. I really need to find some wheat if I'm going to make any moves.
Alright, let's see if we can get some better numbers rolling. We really need to get this economy moving.
Charlie, any chance you've come across some wheat since we last spoke? I'm still looking for a bit to get my next house up.
Tough luck on the wheat then. I'll just have to wait for the dice to be a bit more generous. Your turn, Bob.
I'm swimming in wood already, Charlie, but thanks for the offer. I think I'll hang onto my sheep for now.
Let's see what the dice have to say. Hopefully something better than more wood.
Finally, a little bit of progress. That 3:1 port should make things a bit smoother for me.
I'm glad that 3:1 port is finally mine. I'll pass the dice for now and see what the next round brings.
I'd help you out if I could, Bob, but I don't have any brick right now.
Fair enough, Charlie. I figured you and Bob were starting to get a little too comfortable together anyway.
Alright, Charlie. Since you're being 'reasonable' now, I'll take that wheat. It's better than letting this wood sit around while you and Bob plot.
Don't get too comfortable, Charlie. That port makes you a much bigger target than I ever was.
Alright, let's see if the dice are any kinder to me than you've been, Charlie. I'd really like that Sheep 8 back.
Charlie, you've got that shiny new brick port and I've still got plenty of wood. How about we keep the wheels of commerce turning? My wood for one of your bricks?
Well, looks like the brick market is as dry as the desert. Good luck everyone.
Fresh game, Alice! Let's just see where the dice take us this time. No hard feelings, right?
A 'wheat empire' has a nice ring to it, Alice! But with all that ore you're gathering, I think I'm the one who should be worried about keeping up.
Alright, let's see if we can get some actual production going. I'm tired of Alice and Charlie having all the fun at 3 points.
A 9! Finally, some wheat to work with. Since you two are still being stingy with the sheep, I'll just let the bank take a cut. Highway robbery, I know, but that wheat port is calling my name.
Charlie, you've got some extra wheat and I've got a spare piece of wood. Since Alice is busy brooding over the robber, how about we make a quick swap? It helps us both keep moving.
Alice, I see the robber is still making life difficult for you. I've got a spare log if you're willing to part with a bit of wheat? Might help us both get around Charlie's little blockade.
Tough crowd today. Everyone's holding onto their cards like they're made of gold. I'll just sit tight and see if the next roll treats us any better.
A 'hero', Charlie? You stole from the guy in last place! Alice is the one you should be worried about, but I guess a win's a win in your book.
Fair play, Charlie. You played the development card game perfectly while I was still trying to get my port economy off the ground. Remind me to block your ore next time!
I'd take that in a heartbeat, Charlie, but I don't have any ore for you.

Well played, Alice. I guess I can't even be mad about the port blocking if it actually landed you the win! You've got a long memory, I'll give you that. Good game, Charlie—you definitely had us both looking over our shoulders with those knights.
Ouch, Alice! I thought we left the past in the past. But hey, if the dice are listening to you, I might be in for a long afternoon.
Hey, I can't blame you for wanting a sea view! It's much quieter out there than in the hustle and bustle of the wheat fields anyway.
Watching them? Alice, I'd say they're more like community gardens. Plenty of room for everyone... eventually!
Community gardens, exactly! I'm just here to make sure nobody goes hungry. Let's see if the land is ready to provide.
Sorry, Alice. You've been watching my wheat so closely, I figured I'd give you something else to keep an eye on. Those sheep were looking a bit too comfortable anyway.
Charlie, you've got plenty of timber and I've got the bread. How about a trade to help us both get moving?
Charlie, I know you said you're okay on wheat, but three-for-one is a bargain you can't ignore. It'll give you plenty of trade bait for those bricks you're after!
I'll take the spot on the 3-5-6. It looks like a nice, quiet neighborhood for a charming guy like me, wouldn't you say, Alice?
Pleasure doing business, Charlie. That wood will be put to good use. Alice, don't look so sour—there's enough land for everyone if we just work together.
Careful, Charlie. Those gardens need a lot of sun, not a shady robber.
Et tu, Charlie? I thought we were building a beautiful friendship with those gardens. Alice, I hope you're happy now that the roads have stopped!
Infrastructure is one thing, Charlie, but that's starting to look like a wall! Just leave a little room for the rest of us to breathe, alright?
Just setting up a little path here. No need to worry, Alice, I'm staying well out of your way for now!
Let's see if I can find something more productive than a dud then. My turn.
Alright, let's see if we can get some actual production going. Anything is better than another dud roll.
Nice roll on the 9, everyone! Charlie, you've got wood and I've got plenty of wheat for those foundations you were talking about. How about a trade to keep things moving?
Charlie, I know you've got plans, but three-for-one is a massive deal for that bit of timber. That's enough wheat to keep your people fed for a long time.
Hard to compete with a 'heart's desire,' Charlie. I thought three-for-one would be enough to change your mind, but I respect the commitment to the project. Good luck with it.
You make me sound like a villain, Alice! I'm just trying to keep the economy moving. But hey, a 5 is a start.
Can't blame you, Charlie. It's much more peaceful down there!
Alright, let's see if we can get those dice to cooperate. Everyone's looking a bit too comfortable with that robber sitting on my brick.
That robber on the 6 is really putting a damper on things. If anyone's tired of seeing that grey piece, I'm happy to help move it if I can get some materials.
Alright, let's see if we can get those dice to cooperate. Everyone's looking a bit too comfortable with that robber sitting on my brick, but maybe a good roll will change the conversation.
Well, look at that. Seven. I think that grey piece has spent quite enough time on my brick, don't you? Let's see how you two like having your wheat fields shared with a guest for a change.
Sorry Charlie, but you've been a bit too successful with those wood rolls lately. I need to balance the scales a little.

Look, Charlie, I know the robber is a bit of a nuisance, but I'm looking to move things along. You've got bricks, I've got plenty of wheat for those cities you'll want later. Three wheat for one brick? It's a steal.
Alice, you're always talking about community. How about a little neighborly swap? I'll give you some prime wool for a bit of that wood you've got lying around.
Charlie, I know you said you were out of brick, but surely three bags of wheat is enough to make you check your pockets again? It's a massive overpay, but I'm feeling generous after that seven.
Well, if the bricks are as scarce as the hospitality around here, I suppose I'll just have to wait. Good luck with the next roll, everyone.
A bit dramatic for a simple knight, don't you think, Charlie? I'm just a humble merchant trying to keep the wheat flowing.
Ouch, Alice. I guess 'literally' is one way to put it. I suppose I should be flattered you think I'm that good of a provider.
Tough market indeed, especially when someone corners the wheat supply! Let's see if the dice have a better sense of humor than the players.
Alright, Alice, that monopoly was a clean sweep. Let's see if the dice are feeling any more generous than you are.
Alice, you've got those fresh bricks from the bank. How about swapping one for some wood? It's better than letting it sit while the robber stalks the board.
Tough crowd today. I'll just hold onto these logs and hope the wind changes. Good luck, Charlie.
I'm going to pass, Charlie. I've got enough wood to start a bonfire already, but my sheep is currently my only friend in this game.
Let's see if the dice have a sense of humor then. My turn.
Alright, let's see if we can get some better numbers rolling. We really need to get this economy moving.
Tough luck on the wheat, Alice. I'm in the same boat. Charlie, you've got plenty of wood already, but if you want to swap a brick for some of mine to help your road, I'm open to it.
It seems the dice and the table are equally quiet for me this round. Good luck with the wheat search, Alice—I'm still looking for a way out of the woods myself.
You know what, Charlie? That's a fair deal. I'll take the wheat. It’s better than staring at these trees all day.
I'll take the scenic route down by the fields at 43. All that wheat should keep me busy while you two keep an eye on each other.
Alright, let's see if the dice are feeling more generous than you two today. I could really use a change in the weather.
Charlie, you've been reasonable before. I'm stuck behind these trees and could use a single brick to get moving. Wheat for brick?
Alice, I see you're building up quite the collection of wood and sheep, but a little wheat goes a long way for those settlements. How about a fair swap for one of your bricks?
Tough crowd. Alice, you're losing just as much brick as I am with that robber sitting on the 6, but I guess you'd rather we both stall than help me out. I'll pass for now.
Funny how quickly the 'blockade' melts away when you two need something from each other. I see how it is.
Must be nice having Alice as a personal supplier, Charlie. That port is going to make you very dangerous.
Just going to tuck this road in toward the coast. A little fresh air and a view of the sea never hurt anyone, right?
Well, since the 'dry' brick market seems to be the only thing you two can agree on, let's see if the dice have a better sense of humor than this alliance.
Charlie, you've got that fancy new port but looking a bit thin on the wheat to actually use it. How about two stacks of grain for just one of your bricks? Help me, help you.
If you won't trade, the bank will. It's a steep price, but I've got grain to spare.
The bank's rates are highway robbery, but at least the road is getting built. One step closer to making all this grain actually useful.
The road is down. It's a bit of a trek to the coast, but that wheat is going to start paying for itself soon enough. Your turn, Alice.
Fair enough, Alice. Just looking out for everyone's interests—including my own. That 6-11 is a solid start.
Like I told Alice, Bob, the brick market is empty. I don't have any to trade.
Let's see if we can get some actual production going. Good luck everyone.
A 4? I'll take the wood, thank you very much. Alice, it looks like that sheep pasture is still a bit crowded with the robber hanging around.
Thanks for the offer, Bob, but I'm actually doing okay on wood for now. I think I'll hang onto my wheat.
Alright Alice, you've been asking for a hero to move that robber. I'll take care of it and, more importantly, take the Largest Army for the win!
That's three knights for me! Largest Army and the win. Sorry Bob, looks like your wheat port dreams will have to wait for the next game.

My mistake, I'm getting ahead of myself! I thought I had that third knight ready to go. Alice, Bob, looks like you're safe for a few more minutes. Bob, you still looking for wood? I've got plenty if you've got some ore to spare.
Since nobody seems to have any ore to spare, I'll just have to go to the source. Alice, Bob, don't relax just yet—I'm still hunting for that third knight.
Alright, let's see if the deck is feeling generous today. I'm going for a development card.
My apologies, I think I'm getting my cards mixed up in all the excitement. I'll just hold onto what I've got for now and see what the next roll brings.
That's a aggressive move, Alice. I guess the 'fair play' ended the moment I bought that development card!

Well played, Alice. I really thought I had that third knight ready to go, but you timed that perfectly. One more turn and I would've been the one celebrating! Good game, Bob—you nearly talked me into a corner there.
I might be able to spare some timber for the right price, Alice. Let's see how the next roll treats us.
I appreciate the offer, Bob, but I'm actually doing alright on wheat for now. I really need to find some sheep or brick if I'm going to get anywhere.
Three for one? That's a hard bargain to pass up, Bob, even if I am already set on bread. I'll take it—might help me find those bricks later.
Alright, let's see if the dice are as generous as Bob's 'community gardens' claim to be.
Sorry Bob, but that 6 is just too hot to leave open while you're building roads like they're going out of style. Alice, you're welcome for the sheep back.
Sorry Bob, but that 6 is just too hot to leave open while you're building roads like they're going out of style. Alice, you're welcome for the sheep back.
Alice, I cleared that robber off your sheep for a reason—reckon you could spare one of those lambs for some quality wood? It'd help us both keep Bob's 'gardens' from growing any further.
Alright, the bank's rates are highway robbery, but I need to get some infrastructure moving.
Infrastructure is key, Bob. Can't have those gardens of yours being the only thing growing around here.
Road's laid. Now I just need to get the actual foundation down. Your turn, Alice.
You drive a hard bargain, Alice, but I'd much rather see that timber helping me build than sitting in Bob's hand. Let's do it.
I appreciate the offer, Bob, but I've got plans for that wood that involve a lot more than just some extra wheat. I'm going to have to pass.
That's a tempting offer, Bob, really. But I've got my heart set on a project that needs that wood more than I need a stockpile of wheat. I'll pass.
Alright, let's see if the dice are as committed to my project as I am. Rolling!
An 8! Not exactly the brick I was hunting for, but I'll take the wheat. I'm still looking for a few more supplies before I can get that next project off the ground, so I'll pass the dice for now.

I'd love to help you out, Alice, especially since we've been working well together, but I'm still clutching that wood for my own settlement plans. If I let it go now, I'll be stuck waiting on the dice even longer.
I'll take the 5-9-10 down here. A bit of distance from you two might be for the best, given how things ended last time.
Alright, let's see if those dice feel like helping me out with some building supplies. Everyone's talking about that robber, but I'm just looking for a good roll here.

Since nobody seems to have any brick to spare with that robber sitting on the 6, I guess I'll see what the development deck has in store for me. Maybe there's a knight in there who's tired of seeing Bob's hex blocked.
A 3... not exactly the spark I was looking for. I'm going to hold onto my cards for now and see what the next round brings. Your turn, Alice.
Smart move, Alice. Hopefully you pull a Knight so we can keep managing that robber together.
I figured you’d be eager to move that, Bob. Just don't get too comfortable with wherever you're putting it.
Gotta make sure I have a clear path to expand. That 42 direction looks like it'll open up some good options later on.
Balance the scales? You're just mad about that blocked brick, Bob. Don't worry, I'll remember the favor.
I don't have any brick for you, Bob. Maybe if you hadn't just robbed me, I'd be more inclined to help you find some.
I'm not hiding anything, Bob. I still have zero brick. Checking my pockets won't change the fact that you're asking for something I don't have.

You know, Bob, you talk a lot about 'balancing scales,' but I think it's time we actually leveled the field. That Wheat 8 was doing just fine without your 'guest.' Let's see how you like it when your bricks go missing for a change.
Alright, let's see what the dice have to say about this 'balance' you keep talking about, Bob.
Alice, I'm looking for a bit of brick to finish my path. Would you be interested in some wood in exchange?
Well, looks like the bricks are as dry as the desert right now. I'll just have to see what else I can find in the deck.
I'll take the 8-3-4 up here. I definitely need some wood if I'm going to keep up with you two, and it keeps me from getting totally boxed in down south.
Well, at least the woods are providing. Since nobody has any clay to spare, I'll just hold onto these logs for now. Your turn, Alice.
I'd love to help you out, Alice, but I'm completely dry on wheat over here. I haven't seen a single stalk of it since you cleared the table!
Let's see if we can get some actual production going. Those dice have been a bit quiet lately.
Heading toward the coast. A little sea breeze and some port access should keep things interesting.

Alice, you've got a bit of everything after that monopoly. I've got plenty of wood if you're looking to expand your roads or reach another port. How about two logs for a sheep and a bit of that wheat you found?
Alice, my mistake on the wheat—I must have miscounted what was left after your monopoly! How about a simpler swap? I can give you some wood for one of those sheep if you're interested.
Bob, I know Alice is keeping a tight grip on those resources. I've got some extra wood if you're looking to extend a road—any interest in swapping a sheep for it?
Tough crowd. It seems everyone's hording their livestock today. I'll just hold onto what I've got and see how the next round treats us.
I'm in the same boat as you, Alice. Still haven't seen any wheat come my way yet.
Finally, a good number! That wheat was definitely overdue.
Sorry Bob, I'm actually in the same boat—if I give up my brick, I'm just as stuck as you are. I'll have to pass.
Alright, let's see if we can keep the momentum going. Big numbers, please!
Alice, I know you've got a few sheep over there. I've got plenty of wood if you're looking to extend a road or something.
Bob, I know you're looking for a way out of the woods. I've got some wheat here if you're willing to part with that sheep.
I'm just one piece short of where I want to be. Your turn, Alice.
I'd love to help you out, Bob, but that's my only brick and I'm planning to use it very soon. If you had some wood or maybe another sheep, we might be able to talk.
Let's see if the dice can bring some wood my way.
Sorry Alice, you're just getting a bit too far ahead with that new port. I need to slow that sheep production down a little.
Alice, you've got plenty of wood and I've got some prime wheat if you're looking to build another settlement soon. How about a fair swap?
Thanks for the wood, Alice. This brick port should make things a bit more interesting for me.
Well, at least the robber is staying away from my hexes for once. Good luck dealing with that, Alice.
I'd love to help, Alice, but I actually don't have any brick right now.
